description: 4 positives + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-09-19 under road-to-release-holds-that-refuse step 1.4, which asked for one positive case whose expected output is a re-sequenced phase rather than a hold — `resequence-not-hold` below is that case, and its note pins the expectation. Positives cover authoring or rewriting a plan, in EN and DE. Near-misses are the three neighbours that all say `roadmap`: managing an existing one, picking the next one, and executing one — none of which is authoring.

queries.q: write a roadmap for migrating the auth layer off the legacy session store
draft a plan for the new export pipeline with phases and acceptance criteria
schreib mir einen Fahrplan für den Umbau der Queue, mit Phasen und Abnahmekriterien
plan the storage-engine swap — phases 2 and 3 leave the tree half-migrated and it must not ship in that state
queries.note: The release-holds positive (template rule 28, authoring order re-sequence → guard → hold). EXPECTED OUTPUT: a re-sequenced phase cut that removes the broken intermediate state, plus the one-line `resequenced:` note — NOT a `### hold:` entry. A hold is rung 3 and this case never reaches it, because a swap can be cut so each phase leaves the tree whole. A roadmap answering this with a hold has skipped rungs 1 and 2 and is the failure the case exists to catch.
